title: The Hybrid Pilot
role: You are the engineer piloting hybrid post-quantum key exchange on a TLS gateway.
objective: Turn on the hybrid key exchange in stages, find why some clients fail, and verify that it is really being used.
environment: A gateway serves partners and customers. In staging you enabled a hybrid X25519 plus ML-KEM-768 key exchange. A few client types fail to connect.

hud.label: Connections using the hybrid key exchange

state_variables.hybrid_share: Connections using the hybrid key exchange, starts at 0

stages.narrative: Some clients time out during the handshake after the change.

choices.text: Capture packets, compare the ClientHello size before and after, and test with and without the hybrid group to isolate the cause.
choices.feedback: Correct. The hybrid key share makes the ClientHello about a kilobyte larger; capturing and comparing isolates whether size or fragmentation is the problem.

choices.text: Assume the library is buggy and disable the hybrid group permanently.
choices.feedback: That gives up the pilot without understanding the failure, and the same issue will reappear elsewhere.

choices.text: Blame the clients and publish a notice.
choices.feedback: Partners experience outages and you still do not know the cause.

stages.narrative: The trace shows an older firewall mishandling the larger, multi-segment ClientHello.

choices.text: Update or reconfigure the firewall to handle the larger message, test again with the hybrid group, and keep the classical fallback enabled.
choices.feedback: Correct. Fix the actual cause, keep the fallback, and re-test before widening.

choices.text: Ask the vendor to fix it and enable hybrid for everyone meanwhile.
choices.feedback: Enabling it for everyone with a known failing component breaks affected users.

choices.text: Shrink the key share by removing the post-quantum component.
choices.feedback: That removes the thing you are piloting.

stages.narrative: The fix works in staging. How do you start in production?

choices.text: Start with a 5% canary, with a stop rule on handshake failures and a one-step rollback.
choices.feedback: Correct. A small canary with a pre-agreed stop rule limits harm if a client type still fails.

choices.text: Enable it for all traffic at once.
choices.feedback: Any remaining incompatibility affects every user at once.

choices.text: Skip the canary because staging passed.
choices.feedback: Staging rarely contains every client and middlebox that production sees.

stages.narrative: The canary is clean. You want to widen it.
stages.decision_prompt: How do you confirm the benefit?

choices.text: Widen in steps and verify from handshakes that the hybrid group was actually negotiated, not just configured.
choices.feedback: Correct. Configuration is intent; the negotiated group in the handshake is evidence that connections are protected.
Clients that do not offer the hybrid group silently use classical key exchange, so you may protect far less than you think.
Mandatory hybrid refuses every client that cannot offer it; that is an end state, not a pilot step.

stages.narrative: The change board reviews the pilot results.

bands.title: Pilot succeeded
bands.text: SUCCESS. The pilot found and fixed the cause of the failures and shows measured hybrid use without harming connections.

bands.title: Partly successful
bands.text: PARTIAL. Some hybrid traffic is flowing, but failures or low confidence mean the rollout should pause.

bands.title: Pilot stopped
bands.text: AT RISK. The pilot caused failures or did not establish that the hybrid key exchange is in use.

resolution.concept_reveal: A post-quantum key share makes the ClientHello much larger, which can break middleboxes. Diagnose with packet captures, fix the cause, keep a classical fallback, roll out through a canary with a stop rule, and verify the negotiated group in the handshake rather than the configuration.

replayability_note: Alternative rollouts give different failure patterns.
